    10	# Uniqueness of finite Galois quotients
    11	
    12	Ported from the sibling Algebraic Jacobian project

    14	
    15	The universal `T`-points clause in `IsGaloisQuotient` determines the quotient
    16	scheme uniquely over the base.  This file packages that observation as a
    17	canonical comparison morphism and isomorphism.  The transitivity theorem is the
    18	cocycle engine for gluing affine Galois quotient charts: once two restrictions
    19	are known to be quotients of the same acted scheme, their overlap isomorphism
    20	and every triple-overlap identity follow from uniqueness.
    21	-/

    31	/-- The data asserted by `IsGaloisQuotient`, retained in `Type` so its universal
    32	property can define comparison morphisms. -/
    33	structure GaloisQuotientWitness
    34	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    35	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    36	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
    37	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) where
    38	  e : pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ≅ X
    39	  over : e.hom ≫ f = pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
    40	  equivariant : (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L g).IsEquivariant rho e.hom
    41	  universal : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (t : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
    42	      (h : pullback t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ⟶ X),
    43	      h ≫ f = pullback.snd t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) →
    44	      (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L t).IsEquivariant rho h →
    45	      ∃! v : {v : T ⟶ Y // v ≫ g = t},
    46	        pullbackBaseChange K L g t v.1 v.2 ≫ e.hom = h
    47	
    48	/-- A quotient witness together with the quotient projection induced by its
    49	pinned base-change isomorphism. -/
    50	structure GaloisQuotientWitnessWithProjection
    51	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    52	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    53	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
    54	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
    55	    (q : X ⟶ Y) extends GaloisQuotientWitness rho Y g where
    56	  projection : e.inv ≫ pullback.fst g
    57	    (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) = q

    61	/-- The comparison morphism defined from two specified quotient witnesses. -/
    62	noncomputable def comparison
    63	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    64	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    65	    {rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f}
    66	    {Y₁ Y₂ : Scheme.{u}}
    67	    {g₁ : Y₁ ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)}
    68	    {g₂ : Y₂ ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)}
    69	    (w₁ : GaloisQuotientWitness rho Y₁ g₁)
    70	    (w₂ : GaloisQuotientWitness rho Y₂ g₂) :
    71	    {v : Y₁ ⟶ Y₂ // v ≫ g₂ = g₁} :=
    72	  (w₂.universal Y₁ g₁ w₁.e.hom w₁.over w₁.equivariant).choose

theorem isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)

      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :

      (Sigma.desc (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :=

/-! ## The converse: `hV` is the exact difference, not a convenient extra

A coupling lemma whose hypothesis is stronger than the gap it bridges hides the gap instead of
naming it.  This section rules that out: restricted coverage gives back unrestricted coverage
together with the containment, so `hV` is precisely what separates the two. -/

is logically equivalent to the conclusion.  In particular a lane cannot obtain B-6 for the
restricted atlas — the one the seam consumes — while avoiding the statement that coverage hits
its classes inside `V i`.

The witness is `x ≫ (V i).ι`, whose range is contained in that of `(V i).ι` by construction,
and whose chart value under `f i` is the restricted chart's value at `x` by

      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧

parameter is a divisor degree.  Allowing arbitrarily many indices does not weaken the
arithmetic condition carried by one legal index. -/
theorem exists_nonempty_legal_chart_index_family_iff_isDivisorDegree (n : ℕ) :
    (∃ (ι : Type u) (_ : Nonempty ι) (m : ι → ℕ)
        (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor),

        = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
      ↔ IsDivisorDegree C (n : ℤ) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨ι, hι, m, Z, hdeg⟩
    let i : ι := Classical.choice hι
    exact isDegree_of_chartIndex C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)
  · intro hn
    obtain ⟨m, Z, hdeg⟩ := chartIndex_of_isDegree C hn
    exact ⟨PUnit, inferInstance, fun _ => m, fun _ => Z, fun _ => hdeg⟩

/-- Any pointwise-covering family indexed by legal charts at parameter `n` forces `n` to be
a divisor degree.  In particular, a genus-parameter multi-index atlas cannot be produced
unconditionally by replacing one base-field chart with many base-field charts. -/
theorem isDivisorDegree_of_pointwiseCoverage_legal_chart_index_family
    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (hcov : PointwiseCoverage C f) (n : ℕ) (m : ι → ℕ)
    (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) :
    IsDivisorDegree C (n : ℤ) := by
  let i : ι := Classical.choice (nonempty_index_of_pointwiseCoverage C f hcov)

@@

+
+/-! ## Pointwise coverage and representability -/
+
+/-- The translated rank-one charts cover the sigma extension pointwise.  At a point `t`,
+restrict the degree-zero class to `Spec κ(t)`, use the exact separably-closed translated
+rank-one factorization there, and take the whole residue-field point as the covering source. -/
+theorem picRankOneTranslatedChart_pointwiseCoverage
+    (hopen : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen (divRepAffP1Map C)) :
+    PointwiseCoverage C (fun a : PicRankOneTranslatorIndex (C := C) =>
+      picRankOneTranslatedChart (C := C)
+        (divRankOneOpenDataOfPicRankOneOpen (divRepAffP1Map C) hopen) a) := by
+  apply pointwiseCoverage_of_residueField (C := C)
+  · exact fun a => picRankOneTranslatedChart_isOpenImmersion (C := C) hopen a
+  · intro T s t
+    rcases s with ⟨b, mu⟩
+    let Tbar : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk b
+    let K := Over.testPointField t
+    let p : overSpec k K ⟶ Tbar := Over.testPoint t
+    let muK : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K) := (pic0TypeFunctor C).map p.op mu
+    obtain ⟨a, x, hx⟩ :=
+      exists_picRankOneTranslatedChart_fieldFactorization (C := C) hopen muK
+    let q : (overSpec k K).left := Classical.choice inferInstance
+    refine ⟨(overSpec k K).left, q, p.left, a, x, ?_, ?_⟩
+    · exact Over.testPoint_base t q
+    · calc
+        _ = (⟨(overSpec k K).hom, muK⟩ :
+              (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op (overSpec k K).left)) := hx
+        _ = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map p.left.op ⟨b, mu⟩ := by
+          exact (Over.sigmaExtension_map_left_mk p mu).symm
 
 end
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));

   150	def IsInvariantMatch (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))

   152	    {X' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k'))}
   153	    (rep : (picEt (Scheme.baseChangeField C k')).RepresentableBy X')
   154	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction k k' X'.left X'.hom)
   155	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) : Prop :=
   156	  ∀ c : (picEt (Scheme.baseChangeField C k')).obj (op (baseTest (k' := k') T)),

   162	half, and half of why satisfiability is not content here.

   164	Both sides of the iff quantify over `γ`; with only `γ = 1` present, the left side is

   173	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :

   175	  intro c
   176	  constructor
   177	  · intro _ γ
   178	    obtain rfl : γ = 1 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
   179	    rw [twistTest_one, op_id]
   180	    simp
   181	  · intro _ γ
   182	    obtain rfl : γ = 1 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
   183	    change ((pullbackSemilinearGalAction k k' T.hom).act 1).hom ≫ _
   184	      = _ ≫ (ρ.act 1).hom
   185	    rw [map_one, map_one]
   186	    change (Iso.refl _).hom ≫ _ = _ ≫ (Iso.refl _).hom
   187	    rw [Iso.refl_hom, Category.id_comp, Iso.refl_hom, Category.comp_id]

     8	/-!
     9	# `G1` IS FREE AT THE CANONICAL ACTION: the invariance match, discharged
    10	
    11	`AJC.picrep.etale-rep.invariance`.
    12	
    13	## What this file removes
    14	
    15	`Picard/PicEtDescentGoal.lean` states the descent goal — a `k'`-side representation
    16	of `picEt (C_{k'})` plus a Galois quotient plus `hcov` plus a predicate match
    17	`IsInvariantMatch` yields `(picEt C).RepresentableBy Y` over `k` — and carries that
    18	match as an **explicit undischarged hypothesis**, identified there as what campaign
    19	`G1` owes.
    20	
    21	**At the canonical action it is not a hypothesis at all.** `isInvariantMatch_canonical`
    22	proves `IsInvariantMatch C rep (semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep) T` for
    23	every test `T`, with **no hypothesis beyond `rep` and the curve's own binders**: no
    24	finiteness, no separability, no `IsGalois`, no rational point, no condition on the
    25	Galois group. So `G1` leaves this route, and the descent goal's inputs drop from four
    26	to three: `rep`, the Galois quotient, and `hcov`.
    27	
    28	## Why it is free — the reason, not just the fact
    29	
    30	The two predicates being matched are *not independent conditions on one object*.
    31	`IsInvariantMatch` asks that
    32	
    33	* `(rep.homEquiv.symm c).left` is **equivariant** for the action `ρ`, and
    34	* the transported class is **`Γ`-invariant** for the twist action on `picEt C`
    35	
    36	agree. At the canonical `ρ = semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep`, the
    37	`γ`-component of the action *is* `twistMor C rep γ`, which is **defined** by
    38	transporting the functor action `galoisActionPicEt` along `rep`. So both sides are
    39	images of one and the same functor-level statement, and the match is an identity
    40	rather than a coincidence. Three steps, each free:
    41	
    42	1. `isEquivariant_iff_galTwistMor` — equivariance of the underlying scheme map is the
    43	   same equation read in the slice over `Spec k'` (`Over.OverMorphism.ext` both ways).
    44	   `galTwistMor` is that slice packaging of `pullbackGalMap`, and it is the `k'`-side
    45	   partner of `PicEtGaloisBridge`'s `k`-slice `twistTest` — `twistTest T γ⁻¹` is
    46	   `pullbackGalMap … γ` on underlying schemes, which is *already* recorded as `rfl` at
    47	   `I-1455`, and `twistTest_eq_restrictTest_galTwistMor` is the slice-level form.
    48	2. `homEquiv_twist_comp` — applying `rep.homEquiv` to the square's right-hand side
    49	   gives `(galoisActionPicEt C γ).inv` applied to `rep.homEquiv φ`. This is
    50	   `homEquiv_twistMor` plus **naturality of the action at `φ.op`**, and it is the step
    51	   that makes the whole thing free: `twistMor` was built from that natural
    52	   transformation, so naturality is exactly what un-builds it.
    53	3. `crossBaseIso_galoisActionPicEt_inv` — transporting along `picEt_crossBaseIso`
    54	   turns the inverse action into `picEt C` applied to
    55	   `restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso`, whose components are the **identity** on
    56	   underlying schemes. Iso cancellation; the cross-base identification's own
    57	   `inv_hom_id_app`.
    58	
    59	Composing, equivariance at `γ` is invariance at `γ⁻¹`; quantifying over the group,
    60	which both predicates do, makes them equal. `Gal(k'/k)` is a group, so the
    61	reindexing `γ ↦ γ⁻¹` is a bijection and no hypothesis on it is needed.
    62	
    63	## What this does NOT do
    64	
    65	* It closes **no** `sorry`. `rep` is still the campaign's undischarged output, and
    66	  clause (1) field 1 of `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` is witnessed for **no**
    67	  curve. This file is verified with that theorem as a `sorryAx` control.
    68	* The remaining two inputs of the descent goal are untouched: `IsGaloisQuotient` at a
    69	  glued non-affine `X'` (`pic-f`'s row) and `hcov` at a nontrivial Galois level
    70	  (`pic-a`'s row). Nothing here makes either cheaper.
    71	* It does **not** rescue the non-vacuity problem `PicEtDescentGoal.lean` records for
    72	  the *pair* `(hcov, IsInvariantMatch)`. It resolves that problem for the match by
    73	  removing it — a hypothesis that is never assumed cannot be vacuously satisfied —
    74	  but `hcov`'s only exhibited witness site still trivialises the conclusion, and that
    75	  half is unchanged.
    76	* It does **not** subsume `isInvariantMatch_of_subsingleton`. **An earlier revision of
    77	  this docstring said it did — "the degenerate case of a fact that holds at every
    78	  extension" — and that is false** (fresh-context audit). That lemma quantifies over an
    79	  **arbitrary** action `ρ`; `isInvariantMatch_canonical` **pins** `ρ` to the canonical
    80	  one. Refuted in one line: `isInvariantMatch_canonical rep T` offered against
    81	  `IsInvariantMatch C rep ρ T` for a bound `ρ` is a type mismatch. The two are

    10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
    11	
    12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
    13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
    14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
    15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
    16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
    17	
    18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
    19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
    21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
    22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
    23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
    25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
    27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
    28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
    29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
    30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
    31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
    32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
    33	-/

    48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
    49	
    50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
    51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
    52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
    53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
    54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
    56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    57	
    58	section DegAt
    59	
    60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    61	
    62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
    63	@[simp]
    64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
    65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
    66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
    67	
    68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
    69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
    71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
    72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
    74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
    75	
    76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
    77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
    79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
    80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
    81	  rfl
    82	
    83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
    84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
    85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
    86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
    87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
    89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
    90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
    91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
    92	
    93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
    94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
    95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
    97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
    98	
    99	end DegAt

   101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
   102	
   103	variable (C) in
   104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
   105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
   106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
   107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
   108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   109	    degAt lam t = 0}
   110	  one_mem' := by
   111	    intro K _ _ t
   112	    exact degAt_one t
   113	  mul_mem' := by
   114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
   115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
   116	  inv_mem' := by
   117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
   118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
   119	
   120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
   121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
   122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
   123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
   125	  Iff.rfl
   126	
   127	variable (C) in
   128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
   129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
   130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
   131	points. -/
   132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
   133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
   134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
   135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
   136	
   137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
   138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
   139	@[simp]
   140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
   141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
   142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
   143	  rfl
   144	
   145	variable (C) in
   146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
   147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
   148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
   149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
   150	functor. -/
   151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
   152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
   153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
   154	  map_id T := by
   155	    ext lam U
   156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
   157	  map_comp g h := by
   158	    ext lam U
   159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
   160	
   161	@[simp]
   162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
   163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
   164	  rfl
   165	
   166	@[simp]
   167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
   168	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
   169	    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
   170	  rfl
   171	
   172	variable (C) in
   173	/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
   174	Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
   175	(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/
   176	def pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
   177	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Subgroup C T.unop).subtype
   178	  naturality _ _ _ := rfl
   179	
   180	end
   181	
   182	end AlgebraicGeometry

   194	
   195	/-- **The `Γ`-stable affine neighbourhood theorem** (campaign `G2(a)`, EGA II 4.5.4
   196	pattern): under the orbit-in-affine hypothesis, every point of `X` has a `Γ`-stable
   197	affine open neighbourhood — the content of the gate `HasStableAffineCover`.  See the
   198	module docstring for the pinned route (prime avoidance + norm, with `Γ`-stability
   199	proved at the level of opens by reindexing, bypassing the section-transport wall). -/
   200	theorem exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbitsInAffineOpen [FiniteDimensional K L]
   201	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) [ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen] (x : X) :
   202	    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ ρ.IsStableOpen U := by
   203	  classical
   204	  obtain ⟨U, hxU⟩ := OrbitsInAffineOpen.exists_affineOpen (rho := ρ) x
   205	  -- the whole orbit of `x` meets every translated chart:
   206	  -- `act γ (act τ x) = act (γ * τ) x ∈ U`.
   207	  have horb : ∀ τ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (ρ.act γ).hom.base ((ρ.act τ).hom.base x) ∈ U.1 := by
   208	    intro τ γ
   209	    have h : (ρ.act γ).hom.base ((ρ.act τ).hom.base x) = (ρ.act (γ * τ)).hom.base x := by
   210	      rw [ρ.act_mul_hom γ τ]; rfl
   211	    rw [h]; exact hxU (γ * τ)
   212	  -- prime avoidance: `orbit ⊆ D(s) ⊆ W := ⋂_γ (act γ)⁻¹ U`.
   213	  obtain ⟨s, hs_mem, hs_le⟩ := exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite U.2
   214	    (fun γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (ρ.act γ).hom.base x) hxU
   215	end SemilinearGalAction

   217	/-- **Discharge of the gate `HasStableAffineCover`** (campaign `G2(a)`; this is the
   218	sanctioned instance): for finite Galois `L/K`, a semilinear `Γ`-action whose orbits
   219	lie in affine opens admits a `Γ`-stable affine cover.  The Hironaka trap (module
   220	docstring of `FiniteGaloisQuotient`) shows the orbit hypothesis cannot be dropped;
   221	`HasGaloisQuotient` is instance-free only off the affine locus (discharged there by
   222	`Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean`). -/
   223	instance hasStableAffineCover_of_orbitsInAffineOpen
   224	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
   225	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
   226	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   227	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) [ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen] :
   228	    HasStableAffineCover K L ρ :=
   229	  ⟨fun x => ρ.exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbitsInAffineOpen x⟩
